title: 08. Multi-Agent & Patterns: Layer 7: Advanced RAG Patterns 1/3: What Is This Layer About? · The RAG Evolution — Why Basic RAG Fails …
summary: After retrieving documents, CRAG grades each document for relevance. If docs are bad → it automatically triggers a web search fallback.
objectives: The RAG Evolution — Why Basic RAG Fails

sections.title: What Is This Layer About?
sections.body:
> **Basic RAG just retrieves and generates. Advanced RAG is smarter — it knows WHEN to retrieve, WHAT to retrieve, HOW to verify what it retrieved, and HOW to fix bad retrievals automatically.**
> This layer is what separates a toy RAG demo from a production RAG system.

sections.title: The RAG Evolution — Why Basic RAG Fails
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│              WHY BASIC RAG FAILS IN PRODUCTION                  │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  BASIC RAG PIPELINE:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Query → Embed → Search Vector DB → Top-K Docs → LLM → Answer

  PROBLEM 1: WRONG DOCS RETRIEVED
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Query:  "What is the latest Python version?"
  Retrieved: "Python history article from 2019"
  LLM Answer: "Python 3.7 is the latest" ❌ (OUTDATED + WRONG)
  Basic RAG doesn't CHECK if docs are relevant!

  PROBLEM 2: AMBIGUOUS QUERIES
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Query:  "How do I fix it?"
  What is "it"?? Embedding this short query finds nothing useful.
  Basic RAG doesn't EXPAND or CLARIFY queries!

  PROBLEM 3: MULTI-HOP QUESTIONS
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Query:  "Who created the framework that powers ChatGPT?"
  Step 1 needed: "ChatGPT uses PyTorch"
  Step 2 needed: "PyTorch was created by Meta AI"
  Basic RAG does ONE retrieval — misses the connection!

  PROBLEM 4: NO SELF-AWARENESS
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Query:  "What is 2 + 2?"
  Basic RAG retrieves docs unnecessarily and wastes money.
  Basic RAG doesn't know WHEN retrieval is even needed!

  PROBLEM 5: HALLUCINATION IN GENERATION
  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Even with good docs, LLM sometimes ignores context and
  generates from its own (wrong) knowledge.
  Basic RAG doesn't VERIFY the generated answer!

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  SOLUTION → ADVANCED RAG PATTERNS:

  ✅ CRAG       → Fix bad retrievals automatically
  ✅ Self-RAG   → Decide IF/WHEN retrieval is needed
  ✅ HyDE       → Better queries via hypothetical docs
  ✅ Multi-Hop  → Chain multiple retrievals
  ✅ Fusion RAG → Multiple queries + combine results
  ✅ GraphRAG   → Knowledge graph for relationships
  ✅ Agentic RAG→ Agent controls entire retrieval process
  ✅ Adaptive   → Route to right retrieval strategy
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > After retrieving documents, CRAG **grades each document** for relevance. If docs are **bad** → it automatically triggers a **web search fallback**. If docs are **partially good** → it **filters out the bad parts**. This self-correcting behavior is what makes it "Corrective."

sections.title: How CRAG Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   CRAG COMPLETE FLOW                            │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Query: "What are the new features in Python 3.13?"

  STEP 1: RETRIEVE (same as basic RAG)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Vector DB search → returns 3 docs:
  Doc A: "Python 3.13 features: free-threaded mode, JIT compiler"
  Doc B: "Python 2.7 end of life announcement"
  Doc C: "How to install Python on Windows"

  STEP 2: GRADE EACH DOCUMENT ← NEW IN CRAG
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  For EACH doc, ask LLM:
  "Is this document relevant to the query?"

  Doc A: Grade = CORRECT   (0.95) ✅ Directly answers query
  Doc B: Grade = INCORRECT (0.08) ❌ Wrong Python version
  Doc C: Grade = AMBIGUOUS (0.45) ⚠️  Related but not specific

  STEP 3: DECIDE ACTION BASED ON GRADES
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  ALL docs CORRECT?                                      │
  │  → Use them directly. Generate answer. Done.            │
  │                                                         │
  │  ALL docs INCORRECT? (worst case)                       │
  │  → Discard ALL. Trigger web search for fresh data.      │
  │  → Use web results to generate answer.                  │
  │                                                         │
  │  MIX of CORRECT + INCORRECT/AMBIGUOUS? (most common)   │
  │  → Keep CORRECT docs                                    │
  │  → For AMBIGUOUS docs: decompose → keep useful parts    │
  │  → For INCORRECT docs: replace with web search          │
  │  → Combine all into final context                       │
  └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  STEP 4: KNOWLEDGE REFINEMENT (for AMBIGUOUS docs)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Doc C is AMBIGUOUS → strip irrelevant sentences
  Keep only: "Python installation requires Python.org download"
  Remove:    "Click next 5 times in the wizard..."

  STEP 5: GENERATE ANSWER from corrected context
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Context = [Doc A (correct)] + [Web results] + [Doc C refined]
  LLM generates accurate, grounded answer ✅

  ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  WHY CRAG IS POWERFUL:
  ✅ Never generates from irrelevant docs
  ✅ Automatically finds better sources when needed
  ✅ Handles outdated knowledge bases gracefully
  ✅ Self-correcting — no human intervention needed
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > Self-RAG trains the LLM to **reflect** on its own outputs using **special tokens**. The agent decides: Should I retrieve? Are these docs relevant? Is my answer supported? Is my answer useful? This creates a **fully self-aware** RAG system.

sections.title: How Self-RAG Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                   SELF-RAG COMPLETE FLOW                        │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  SELF-RAG USES 4 SPECIAL REFLECTION TOKENS:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  [Retrieve]  = Should I search for documents?
                YES → search  |  NO → answer from memory

  [IsRel]     = Is this retrieved document relevant?
                RELEVANT → use it  |  IRRELEVANT → discard

  [IsSup]     = Is my answer supported by the context?
                FULLY → keep  |  PARTIALLY → note uncertainty
                NOT → regenerate more carefully

  [IsUse]     = Is my final answer useful to the user?
                USEFUL(5) → return  |  NOT USEFUL(1) → redo

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  EXAMPLE 1: Question that DOESN'T need retrieval
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Query: "What is 15 * 24?"

  [Retrieve] = NO  ← LLM knows this from training
  Answer:    "15 × 24 = 360"
  [IsSup]    = FULLY ← It's math, no docs needed
  [IsUse]    = 5     ← Perfect answer
  Return:    "15 × 24 = 360" ✅

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  EXAMPLE 2: Question that DOES need retrieval
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Query: "What is GPT-4o's context window size?"

  [Retrieve] = YES ← LLM unsure of exact spec
       ↓
  Retrieved Doc A: "GPT-4o supports up to 128K context tokens"
  [IsRel] = RELEVANT ✅

  Retrieved Doc B: "GPT-3 had a 4K token context window"
  [IsRel] = IRRELEVANT ❌ (wrong model, discard)

  Generate answer using Doc A:
  "GPT-4o has a 128K token context window"

  [IsSup] = FULLY ← Doc A directly states this
  [IsUse] = 5     ← Precise, direct answer
  Return: "GPT-4o has a 128K token context window" ✅

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  EXAMPLE 3: Answer not fully supported
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Query: "Who is the current CEO of OpenAI and their net worth?"

  Retrieved Doc: "Sam Altman is CEO of OpenAI since 2019"
  [IsRel] = RELEVANT (for CEO part)

  Draft answer: "Sam Altman is CEO of OpenAI with net worth $2B"
  [IsSup] = PARTIALLY ← CEO confirmed, net worth not in doc
  [IsUse] = 3         ← Partially useful

  Action: Retrieve again for net worth
  → New doc found → regenerate complete supported answer ✅
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > Instead of embedding the **query** directly (which is often short and vague), HyDE first **generates a hypothetical perfect answer**, then embeds THAT. The hypothetical answer is much richer and more specific → much better retrieval matches.

sections.title: How HyDE Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    HyDE COMPLETE FLOW                           │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  THE PROBLEM WITH DIRECT QUERY EMBEDDING:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Query:  "memory in agents"       ← short, vague, 3 words
  Embedding: [0.2, 0.5, 0.1, ...]  ← weak signal

  HYDE APPROACH:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  STEP 1: GENERATE HYPOTHETICAL DOCUMENT
  The LLM writes what the PERFECT answer would look like:

  Query: "memory in agents"
          ↓
  Hypothetical Doc (LLM-generated):
  "AI agents use multiple types of memory. Short-term memory
   stores recent conversation turns in context window.
   Long-term memory uses vector databases for persistent
   storage across sessions. Episodic memory records past
   agent actions and their outcomes. Semantic memory stores
   factual knowledge as embeddings. Working memory manages
   the active information during task execution..."

  STEP 2: EMBED THE HYPOTHETICAL DOC (not the query!)
  Embedding: [0.45, 0.72, 0.38, ...] ← RICH signal!

  STEP 3: SEARCH VECTOR DB WITH HYPOTHETICAL EMBEDDING
  Finds documents with similar DETAILED content
  → Much better matches than embedding 3 vague words!

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  WHY HyDE WORKS — VISUAL COMPARISON:

  DIRECT QUERY:                    HyDE:
  ───────────────────────          ───────────────────────────
  "memory in agents"               "AI agents use multiple
  Vector: weak, vague              types of memory. Short-term
                                   memory stores recent..."
                                   Vector: rich, detailed

  DB Doc: "Agent memory            DB Doc: "Agent memory
  systems explained"               systems explained"
  Similarity: 0.62 ⚠️              Similarity: 0.91 ✅

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  BEST USE CASES FOR HyDE:
  ✅ Short, ambiguous queries      ("memory in agents")
  ✅ Technical/specialized topics  (LLM knows the domain)
  ✅ When your knowledge base has  long detailed documents
  ❌ Avoid when:                   LLM doesn't know the topic
                                   (hallucinated HyDoc = bad retrieval)
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > Some questions require **chaining multiple retrievals**. The answer from retrieval 1 reveals what to search for in retrieval 2, and so on. Like following a trail of breadcrumbs to the final answer.

sections.title: How Multi-Hop Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  MULTI-HOP RAG COMPLETE FLOW                    │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  QUESTION: "What programming language was used to build
             the framework that Meta used to train LLaMA?"

  This needs 3 hops. Single retrieval would FAIL.

  HOP 1: Retrieve answer to: "What framework did Meta use for LLaMA?"
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Retrieved: "Meta trained LLaMA using PyTorch framework"
  Can we answer the final question? NO — we still need language.
  New sub-question: "What language is PyTorch written in?"

  HOP 2: Retrieve answer to: "What language is PyTorch written in?"
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Retrieved: "PyTorch is written in Python and C++"
  Can we answer the final question? YES!

  FINAL ANSWER:
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  "Meta used PyTorch (written in Python/C++) to train LLaMA."

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  THE MULTI-HOP ALGORITHM:

  current_question = original_question
  collected_context = []

  LOOP (max 5 hops):
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │  1. Retrieve docs for current_question               │
    │  2. Add retrieved docs to collected_context          │
    │  3. Ask: "Can we answer ORIGINAL question now?"      │
    │     YES → break loop, generate final answer          │
    │     NO  → extract: "What do we still need to know?"  │
    │           Set current_question = new sub-question    │
    │           Continue loop                              │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  Generate final answer using ALL collected_context

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  MULTI-HOP vs SINGLE-HOP:

  Question: "Who founded the company that makes the LLM used in GitHub Copilot?"

  SINGLE-HOP:
  Retrieves: "GitHub Copilot uses GPT models"
  Answer: "I don't have enough information" ❌

  MULTI-HOP:
  Hop 1: "GitHub Copilot uses OpenAI GPT models" ✅
  Hop 2: "OpenAI was co-founded by Sam Altman, Elon Musk, Greg Brockman" ✅
  Answer: "OpenAI (founded by Sam Altman et al.) makes the models for GitHub Copilot" ✅
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > Fusion RAG generates **multiple different versions** of the query, retrieves documents for **each version**, then **fuses and reranks** all results. More query angles = more relevant docs found = better answers.

sections.title: How Fusion RAG Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  FUSION RAG COMPLETE FLOW                       │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  ORIGINAL QUERY: "How do I make my RAG system faster?"

  STEP 1: GENERATE MULTIPLE QUERY VERSIONS
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Original:   "How do I make my RAG system faster?"
  Version 2:  "RAG performance optimization techniques"
  Version 3:  "Reducing latency in retrieval augmented generation"
  Version 4:  "Speed improvements for vector search pipelines"

  WHY: Each version finds DIFFERENT relevant docs!

  STEP 2: RETRIEVE FOR EACH VERSION (in parallel)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Original  → [Doc A, Doc B, Doc C, Doc D, Doc E]
  Version 2 → [Doc B, Doc F, Doc G, Doc H, Doc I]
  Version 3 → [Doc A, Doc C, Doc J, Doc K, Doc L]
  Version 4 → [Doc F, Doc M, Doc N, Doc O, Doc P]

  STEP 3: RECIPROCAL RANK FUSION (RRF)
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Each document gets a score based on its RANK in each list.
  RRF Score = Σ 1/(k + rank)  where k=60 (constant)

  Doc A: rank 1 in Original + rank 3 in Version 3
         = 1/(60+1) + 1/(60+3) = 0.0164 + 0.0159 = 0.0323

  Doc B: rank 2 in Original + rank 1 in Version 2
         = 1/(60+2) + 1/(60+1) = 0.0161 + 0.0164 = 0.0325

  Doc F: rank 5 in Version 2 + rank 1 in Version 4
         = 1/(60+5) + 1/(60+1) = 0.0154 + 0.0164 = 0.0318

  RANKING AFTER FUSION:
  1. Doc B  (0.0325) ← appeared in 2 query versions at top
  2. Doc A  (0.0323) ← appeared in 2 query versions
  3. Doc F  (0.0318) ← appeared in 2 query versions
  4. Doc C  (0.0210) ← appeared in 1 version
  ...

  STEP 4: USE TOP RERANKED DOCS → Generate answer
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  Docs that appear across MULTIPLE query versions = more relevant!
  RRF naturally surfaces the most universally relevant docs.

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  FUSION RAG vs BASIC RAG:

  Basic RAG: 1 query → 5 docs → some might miss the point
  Fusion RAG: 4 queries → 20 docs → reranked → top 5
              Much better coverage, much better answers!
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > GraphRAG builds a **knowledge graph** from your documents — entities become **nodes**, relationships become **edges**. When you query, it traverses the graph to find **connected knowledge** that flat vector search would miss.

sections.title: How GraphRAG Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  GRAPHRAG COMPLETE FLOW                         │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  INDEXING PHASE: Build Knowledge Graph from Documents
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Document: "LangChain was created by Harrison Chase. It uses
             LangGraph for multi-agent workflows. LangGraph
             builds on top of LangChain's LCEL syntax."

  ENTITIES EXTRACTED:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  LangChain   [Framework]                                 │
  │  Harrison Chase  [Person]                                │
  │  LangGraph   [Framework]                                 │
  │  LCEL        [Syntax/Tool]                               │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  RELATIONSHIPS EXTRACTED:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Harrison Chase ──CREATED──→ LangChain                   │
  │  LangChain      ──USES──────→ LangGraph                  │
  │  LangGraph      ──BUILDS_ON→ LCEL                        │
  │  LangGraph      ──PART_OF──→ LangChain                   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  KNOWLEDGE GRAPH VISUAL:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │                                                          │
  │  Harrison Chase ──CREATED──→ [LangChain]                 │
  │                                  │                       │
  │                              USES│                       │
  │                                  ▼                       │
  │                            [LangGraph]                   │
  │                                  │                       │
  │                          BUILDS_ON│                      │
  │                                  ▼                       │
  │                              [LCEL]                      │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  QUERY PHASE: Graph Traversal
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Query: "What is the relationship between Harrison Chase and LangGraph?"

  VECTOR SEARCH alone might MISS this:
  → "Harrison Chase" in doc 1
  → "LangGraph" in doc 3
  → No direct connection found ❌

  GRAPH TRAVERSAL finds it:
  → Find node: "Harrison Chase"
  → Follow CREATED edge → "LangChain"
  → Follow USES edge → "LangGraph"
  → Path: Harrison Chase → LangChain → LangGraph ✅

  Answer: "Harrison Chase created LangChain, which uses
           LangGraph for multi-agent workflows."

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  VECTOR RAG vs GRAPH RAG:

  ┌───────────────────┬────────────────┬────────────────────┐
  │  Question Type    │  Vector RAG    │  Graph RAG         │
  ├───────────────────┼────────────────┼────────────────────┤
  │ "What is X?"      │  ✅ Great       │  ✅ Great          │
  │ "Who created X?"  │  ✅ Good        │  ✅ Great          │
  │ "How are X and Y  │  ❌ Often misses│  ✅ Perfect        │
  │  related?"        │                │                    │
  │ "What connects    │  ❌ Very hard   │  ✅ Natural        │
  │  A to D via B,C?" │                │                    │
  │ "What does X      │  ⚠️  Partial    │  ✅ Complete       │
  │  depend on?"      │                │                    │
  └───────────────────┴────────────────┴────────────────────┘
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > An **agent** fully controls the retrieval process. It decides: what to search, how many times to search, when to stop, how to combine results. Unlike passive RAG (retrieve once), Agentic RAG is **iterative and dynamic**.

sections.title: How Agentic RAG Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                  AGENTIC RAG COMPLETE FLOW                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  PASSIVE RAG (basic):                AGENTIC RAG:
  ─────────────────────────           ────────────────────────────
  Query → Retrieve → Generate         Agent THINKS → Decides →
  (1 retrieval, done)                 Retrieves → Evaluates →
                                      Retrieves again if needed →
                                      Generates → Validates →
                                      Done (or tries again)

  EXAMPLE: "Compare LangGraph and AutoGen for building
            customer service bots"

  PASSIVE RAG:
  Retrieves "LangGraph docs" → generates (misses AutoGen) ❌

  AGENTIC RAG:
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Think: "I need info on both. Let me search separately." │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           ↓
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Action 1: search("LangGraph features customer service") │
  │  Result:   "LangGraph: stateful, human-in-loop, graph"   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           ↓
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Action 2: search("AutoGen features customer service")   │
  │  Result:   "AutoGen: multi-agent conversations, group"   │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           ↓
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Think: "Do I have enough for comparison? Let me check." │
  │  Evaluate: LangGraph ✅ | AutoGen ✅ | Comparison ❓      │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           ↓
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Action 3: search("LangGraph vs AutoGen comparison")     │
  │  Result:   "LangGraph better for stateful, AutoGen       │
  │             better for conversational multi-agent"        │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           ↓
  ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  Think: "Now I have enough. Generating comprehensive     │
  │          comparison answer."                             │
  └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
           ↓
  FINAL ANSWER: Complete, accurate comparison ✅

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  AGENTIC RAG TOOLS:

  retrieve(query)     → semantic search in vector DB
  web_search(query)   → real-time web search
  verify(claim, docs) → check if answer is supported
  refine_query(q)     → make query more specific
  check_coverage()    → are all aspects of question answered?
```

sections.title: What Is It?
sections.body: > Adaptive RAG **classifies the query** first, then **routes** it to the most appropriate retrieval strategy. Simple questions → no retrieval. Single-doc questions → basic RAG. Complex multi-doc questions → advanced RAG. The right tool for each job.

sections.title: How Adaptive RAG Works
sections.body:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                 ADAPTIVE RAG COMPLETE FLOW                      │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

  STEP 1: CLASSIFY QUERY COMPLEXITY
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  QUERY TYPE          DESCRIPTION              STRATEGY
  ─────────────────   ───────────────────────  ─────────────────
  No Retrieval        LLM knows it             Answer directly
  Single-Hop Simple   One doc answers it       Basic RAG
  Single-Hop Complex  One doc, needs analysis  RAG + reasoning
  Multi-Hop           Multiple docs needed     Multi-Hop RAG
  Real-Time           Needs current data       Web search RAG
  Comparison          Multiple perspectives    Fusion RAG
  Relationship        Entity connections       Graph RAG

  STEP 2: ROUTE TO CORRECT STRATEGY
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

  Query: "What is 2+2?"
  Classify: NO_RETRIEVAL (pure math)
  Route:    Answer directly → "4" ✅

  Query: "What is LangChain?"
  Classify: SINGLE_HOP_SIMPLE
  Route:    Basic RAG → retrieve 1 doc → answer ✅

  Query: "What is the relationship between LangChain
          and OpenAI's function calling?"
  Classify: MULTI_HOP
  Route:    Multi-Hop RAG → 2-3 retrievals ✅

  Query: "Compare LangGraph vs AutoGen vs CrewAI"
  Classify: COMPARISON
  Route:    Fusion RAG → multiple queries → merge ✅

  Query: "What are the latest AI releases this week?"
  Classify: REAL_TIME
  Route:    Web Search RAG → live data ✅

  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  WHY ADAPTIVE RAG MATTERS:

  ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
  │  WITHOUT Adaptive:                                        │
  │  ALL queries go through FULL RAG pipeline                 │
  │  "What is 2+2?" → embed → search → retrieve → generate   │
  │  Wastes: time + money + context window                    │
  │                                                           │
  │  WITH Adaptive:                                           │
  │  "What is 2+2?"    → no retrieval  → instant + $0.001    │
  │  "What is X?"      → basic RAG     → fast + $0.01        │
  │  "Compare X and Y" → Fusion RAG    → thorough + $0.05    │
  │  "How are X,Y,Z connected?" → GraphRAG → deep + $0.08    │
  └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```
